hint.workingmedium.certified: Certificate written to the output slots.
hint.workingmedium.clogged: Empty the output slots or tanks. Every output of a batch must fit before it runs.
hint.workingmedium.coking: Sneak-use the controller to clear the coke, then keep the cracker cooler.
hint.workingmedium.flood: Every tray needs a side hatch connected to something.
hint.workingmedium.frozen: Sneak-use the controller to thaw, then keep the cold end colder.
hint.workingmedium.idle: No recipe matches the inputs. Check items, fluids and the minimum size.
hint.workingmedium.leak: Put a seal in the seal slot. Higher-grade seals last longer.
hint.workingmedium.missing_part: Add trays, bays, stages or coils, or put an electrode in the electrolyzer special slot.
hint.workingmedium.no_air: The shell does not hold enough air. Add flow.
hint.workingmedium.no_drain: Add a drain hatch. Recipes that produce acid, chlorine, caustic or flue gas will not start without one.
hint.workingmedium.no_lube: Pipe lubricant into any fluid hatch or the controller; it goes to the lubricant tank.
hint.workingmedium.no_vent: Add a relief hatch before running a hot recipe in a large vessel.
hint.workingmedium.paused: A redstone signal is holding this machine. Remove the signal to start it again. Air, lubricant and the seal are not spent while it is paused.
hint.workingmedium.pressure: Raise or lower the shell pressure. A regulator skid or reducer helps hold a narrow band.
hint.workingmedium.running: Working. A comparator next to the controller still reads batch progress if you pause the machine.
hint.workingmedium.scrapped: The batch left its window and was lost. Stabilize before the next one.
hint.workingmedium.temperature: Add heat or cold through the shell, coils or a heat gallery.
hint.workingmedium.unformed: Check the JEI structure page: controller facing, casing grade and hatch positions.
hint.workingmedium.window: Inside the window. Keep pressure and temperature where they are.
jei.workingmedium.held: Stays in the machine, not consumed
jei.workingmedium.info.asphalt: The residue kiln lays this from oil, and four stone dust plus one heavy wax also craft four blocks of it. It is a paved road: walking on it is 35% faster than on stone.
jei.workingmedium.info.certificate: The calibration bench writes a new certificate each time it watches three different machines stay inside their windows long enough. Bind each machine with the Venturi Probe, then use the probe on the bench. Use a certificate on a formed machine that spends air, a column, a charging station, a regulator or a fluid loop. Certified regulators waste less air; certified loops move more fluid; certified columns and charging pads spend 25% less air for the same output. Item galleries, heat galleries, flares and the bench itself will not take a certificate.
jei.workingmedium.info.chip: Lamination produces a dirty microfluidic chip. The clean room washes it under pure nitrogen. The critical kettle must hold a cleaned chip (it is not consumed) to make a critical core.
jei.workingmedium.info.cryo_fluid: Standing in this cold fluid freezes you and slows you down. Keep liquid carbon dioxide, nitrogen, argon and oxygen in tanks and pipes. Oxygen will also feed a fire that is already burning. Creative and spectator modes are not affected.
jei.workingmedium.info.cylinder: Place a cylinder in the special slot of a compressor or expander column to multiply how much air it moves. Higher grades move more (G2 is twice the base rate, G5 is five times).
jei.workingmedium.info.diaphragm: Place a diaphragm in the special slot of a regulator skid to keep more of the inlet air. Without one, 80% reaches the outlet; a G2 diaphragm keeps 84%, a G5 keeps 96%.
jei.workingmedium.info.electrode: The electrolyzer will not run without an electrode in the special slot. A fresh electrode lasts 64 batches and takes damage instead of being consumed whole. Item input hatches also route electrodes to that slot.
jei.workingmedium.info.flammable_fluid: Hydrogen ignites if you are already on fire, or if fire, lava, magma, a lit campfire or a lava cauldron is next to the pool. A spilled pool next to a flame burns off and may leave fire behind. Keep it in tanks and pipes, or burn it in the flare or the cycle island. Creative and spectator modes are not affected.
jei.workingmedium.info.flare: The flare burns hydrogen, flue gas, acid mist, chlorine and dusty steam, and dumps that heat into its shell. It will not burn nitrogen, argon, oxygen, pure nitrogen or inerts. A nozzle in the special slot multiplies the burn rate.
jei.workingmedium.info.gauge: Joins the air network. Sneak-use picks the grade it judges. A comparator reads 0 when empty and 15 at that grade's safe pressure.
jei.workingmedium.info.gripper: Place a gripper in the special slot of a charging station or drone nest to multiply how fast it charges. Higher grades charge more (G2 is twice the base rate, G5 is five times).
jei.workingmedium.info.hatch_drain: A drain hatch only lets fluid out of the output tanks. Recipes that produce acid, chlorine, caustic or flue gas will not start unless the structure has a drain hatch. A comparator on the drain reads how full the output tanks are.
jei.workingmedium.info.hatch_gauge: A gauge hatch outputs the same comparator signal as its bound controller, so you can read batch progress or shell pressure from a hatch on the structure.
jei.workingmedium.info.hatch_heat: A heat hatch exposes the bound controller's heat exchanger, so PneumaticCraft heat pipes can connect to the structure instead of only the controller block. It also outputs a comparator signal for the shell temperature, from empty at -200 C to full at 1500 C.
jei.workingmedium.info.hatch_io: Item, fluid and gas hatches output a comparator signal for how full they are: item-in hatches read the input row, item-out and drain hatches read the output row. A gas hatch counts only gases in the input tanks; a fluid hatch counts only liquids. A gas hatch also only drains gases from the output tanks, and a fluid hatch only drains liquids. The drain hatch still yields every output. Heat hatches report shell temperature instead.
jei.workingmedium.info.hazard_fluid: Standing in this fluid hurts you. Chlorine and acid mist also inflict poison. Recipes that produce these fluids need a drain hatch or the machine will not start. Keep them in tanks and pipes, or burn hydrogen, flue gas, acid mist, chlorine and dusty steam in the flare. Nitrogen, argon, oxygen and inerts will not burn.
jei.workingmedium.info.nozzle: Place a nozzle in the special slot of a flare stack to multiply how much waste gas it burns each tick. Higher grades burn more (G2 is twice the base rate, G5 is five times). The flare also heats its shell while it burns. It only accepts hydrogen, flue gas, acid mist, chlorine and dusty steam.
jei.workingmedium.info.oxidizer_fluid: Oxygen still freezes and slows you, but if you are already on fire it feeds the flames. Keep it in tanks and pipes. Creative and spectator modes are not affected.
jei.workingmedium.info.plasticizer: The lube mixer turns heavy wax and water into plasticizer. Feeding it to the polymerizer with a catalyst raises the engineering plastic yield from 2 to 3.
jei.workingmedium.info.probe: The Venturi Probe stores a machine for the calibration bench. Use it on a bound hatch to store that controller. Use it on a reducer, booster, relief valve or gauge to read the current pressures.
jei.workingmedium.info.program_sheet: Used to laminate a microfluidic chip. In the drone nest's special slot, the nest also charges pneumatic items and grade drills lying within four blocks of the pad.
jei.workingmedium.info.pump: Place a vane pump in the special slot of a fluid loop to multiply how much fluid it transfers each tick. Higher grades move more (G2 is twice the base rate, G5 is five times).
jei.workingmedium.info.purge: If a machine has nitrogen, argon, inerts or pure nitrogen in an input tank, and the current recipe does not consume that gas, it slowly uses the gas as a purge and the seal wears half as fast.
jei.workingmedium.info.redstone_pause: A redstone signal pauses this block: a reducer or booster stops transferring air, and a relief valve stops venting. The air connections stay in the network. Formed machine controllers already pause the same way.
jei.workingmedium.info.scald_fluid: Standing in dusty steam scalds you. It can still leave through a normal fluid or gas hatch; recipes that make it do not need a drain hatch. Creative and spectator modes are not affected.
jei.workingmedium.info.seal: Goes in the seal slot of any machine from G1 up; item input hatches also route seals there. G0 machines such as the impact crusher do not wear seals and will not leak for want of one. A seal is fitted when the old one drops below 800. G2 seals last 1000 running ticks, G3 1500, G4 2000, G5 2500.
jei.workingmedium.info.slide: Place a slide in the special slot of an item gallery to multiply how many items it moves. Higher grades move more (G2 is twice the base rate, G5 is five times).
jei.workingmedium.info.stone_dust: The impact crusher can break cobblestone, stone, gravel, deepslate, cobbled deepslate, blackstone, netherrack, andesite, diorite, granite, tuff, basalt, calcite or end stone into stone dust, besides the dust that comes off crushed ore. Netherrack also yields a gold nugget. Silk-touched iron, copper and gold ore (including deepslate and nether gold) crush into two crushed ore. Silk-touched coal, redstone, lapis, diamond, emerald and nether quartz ore also crush into a bonus of that drop, and glowstone, amethyst blocks and quartz blocks break back into four pieces. Four dust crafts back into cobblestone. Four dust plus heavy wax crafts four asphalt. The lube mixer wets four dust with water to make two clay balls. The washer can also rinse gravel with water into flint and stone dust.
jei.workingmedium.info.waste_chip: If the clean room airlock opens or the pressure leaves 0.15-2.5 bar during a run, the wafer in progress is scrapped. Four scrap wafers sinter back into a substrate. Eight scrap wafers still trade for an emerald at the byproduct catalog.
jei.workingmedium.structure.hatches: Hatches may replace casings in the shell. Same-grade casings connect visually.
jei.workingmedium.structure.optional.ket: Heat coils inside the vessel are optional and are not shown here. Hot or cryogenic recipes need one or two coils.
jei.workingmedium.structure.optional.tow: Side hatches on each tray are not in this minimum schematic. A tray without a side hatch floods and the tower stops, but the structure still forms.
manual.workingmedium.page.0: Working Medium keeps PneumaticCraft's air network and adds grades. Pressure and flow are different. Temperature is a second limit. The working medium itself changes: air, oil cuts, nitrogen, argon, then supercritical carbon dioxide.
manual.workingmedium.page.1: G0 is 5 bar. G1 is 10. G2 is 20. G3 is 50 and needs industrial tube. G4 is 120 and needs cryogenic tube. A weak tube on a strong line explodes. G5 is not higher: the kettle must sit at 70-80 bar and 25-40 C. Outside that window the batch is scrap.
manual.workingmedium.page.10: The cryo tower wants flue gas and a cold coil. Eight trays split inerts, nitrogen, argon, oxygen and liquid carbon dioxide. Ten trays make pure nitrogen. If the cold end is lost, carbon dioxide freezes mid-tower; sneak-use thaws it. Any full outlet stops the whole tower. The clean room is a 7x7x7 hollow shell (5-wide interior) and wants that pure nitrogen and a small positive pressure. Opening the airlock with redstone, or leaving 0.15-2.5 bar mid-run, scraps the wafer into a scrap wafer.
manual.workingmedium.page.11: Lamination at 16-19 bar does not come off the 20 bar main. Use the regulator skid. The long gallery, pure nitrogen and argon make a microfluidic chip, and the last step consumes a drone sheet crafted from a drone; place that sheet in the program slot. The chip leaves the gallery dirty. The clean room washes it under pure nitrogen; the critical kettle must hold that cleaned chip (it stays in the machine) as well as liquid carbon dioxide, and it must sit at 70-80 bar and 25-40 C. Leaving that window scraps the batch and yields no critical core. The calibration bench watches three machines. Bind each with the probe, then use the probe on the bench. Hold the window long enough and it writes the certificate. Scrap wafers sell eight-for-one emerald at the byproduct catalog. Drone pieces: workingmedium_read_gauge runs once and stores pressure times 100, celsius and a window flag in the coordinate variable %wm_reading. workingmedium_hold_window stays only while the machine is inside the window. Copper and gold follow iron through the washer and the thermolysis kettle, and each of those recipes has a non-target output.
manual.workingmedium.page.12: Byproducts have sinks now. The scrubber tower neutralizes acid mist with caustic into brine, and can also neutralize hydrochloric acid the same way. The cyclone splits dusty steam into water and stone dust. The electrolyzer wins copper and gold nuggets from byproduct solution and gives back some hydrochloric acid; its electrode now lasts sixty-four batches instead of one. The same cell recombines hydrogen and chlorine into hydrochloric acid, and it can split water into hydrogen and oxygen without making chlorine. The impact crusher crushes slag into stone dust and an iron nugget. The residue kiln roasts two filter cakes into metal ash and iron nuggets. The cycle island burns diesel or hydrogen with oxygen and actually charges its shell with compressed air; it can also burn crude oil, and oil with oxygen makes more air and less flue gas. Engineering plastic and a circuit board craft two substrates.
manual.workingmedium.page.13: Automation. Item input hatches send seals, catalyst, electrodes, drone sheets, pumps, slides, nozzles, cylinders, diaphragms and grippers to their own slots. A certificate left in an input slot applies itself. Lubricant piped into any fluid hatch fills the lubricant tank. A redstone signal on a formed controller pauses the machine: no air, lubricant or seal is spent until the signal drops. Sneak-use on a formed controller no longer rotates it; sneak-use still clears coke or freeze, and still cycles a regulator setpoint. If the shell breaks mid-batch, the progress and recipe are kept so you can repair it and finish. A comparator on a recipe controller reads batch progress; on storage, columns and regulators it reads shell pressure. A gauge gives a comparator signal against the grade it judges. A batch only starts when all its outputs fit. Breaking a controller drops its contents. The regulator skid bleeds off pressure above its setpoint. Hover the status text in a machine for a hint and the active window. Columns and the regulator skid use their back face only to draw or return air; it does not join the network, so they can hold a pressure different from their source.
manual.workingmedium.page.14: Certificates, upgrades and hatches. The calibration bench writes a new certificate each time it watches three different machines stay in window long enough; use one on a formed machine, or let the machine take it from an input slot, to cut air use and seal wear by 25%. A vane pump in a fluid loop, or a slide in an item gallery, multiplies throughput by its grade; the gallery now moves that many items in one step and shows clogged when the output row is full. Gas hatches only accept gases and only drain gases; fluid hatches only accept and drain liquids (lubricant still goes to the lube tank either way). A gas hatch's comparator reads the fuller of the input and output gases, and a fluid hatch does the same for liquids, so you can time extraction as well as filling. Heat hatches take heat pipes and also output a comparator signal for shell temperature. Gauge hatches output a comparator signal. The Venturi Probe can read a reducer, booster, relief valve or gauge, and a bound hatch stores that controller for the calibration bench. Breaking a controller drops full buckets of its fluids as well as its items. A charging station or drone nest moves a full item into the output row, and shows not enough flow when it has something to charge but the shell is short of air. Four scrap wafers sinter back into a substrate. Sintering metal ash under inert gas yields two catalysts. Asphalt from the residue kiln, or from four stone dust and a piece of heavy wax, is a fast road.
manual.workingmedium.page.15: Parts, heat and hazards. A nozzle in the flare, a cylinder in a compressor or expander, a diaphragm in the regulator, or a gripper in a charging station or drone nest all multiply that machine's work by their grade. A diaphragm also cuts the air the regulator wastes (G2 keeps 84%, G5 keeps 96%; the base is 80%). A certificate on a regulator or fluid loop also helps: less waste, or more flow. The regulator skid can now be set to 80 bar or 120 bar as well as the lower steps, so it can feed a fluid loop or a G4 line. A program sheet in the drone nest also charges pneumatic items and grade drills lying within four blocks of the pad. A charging station or drone nest charges a grade drill at one point per tick at the base rate; a gripper speeds that up, and a drill in a slot no longer fills in a single tick. The pad will use the air it still has, even if the shell is below 500 air, so long as one step can be paid. The heat gallery is a real heat pipe between its two ends. Chlorine, acid mist, hydrochloric acid, caustic, acid feed and flue gas hurt anything that stands in them; chlorine and acid mist also poison. Dusty steam scalds. Hydrogen ignites if you are already on fire or a flame is next to the pool, including a lit campfire or a lava cauldron, and a spilled pool next to fire burns off. Oxygen still freezes, but if you are already on fire the fire burns hotter. Liquid carbon dioxide, nitrogen, argon and oxygen freeze and slow anything that stands in them. A recipe that lists a negative air value, such as the cycle island, produces air rather than consuming it. The island also burns kerosene, gasoline, LPG, crude oil, monomer and plasticizer, and any of the fuels with oxygen makes still more air and less flue gas.
manual.workingmedium.page.16: Automation and cover gas. A paused recipe machine still reports its batch progress to a comparator, so a pause will not look like a finished batch. Item, fluid, gas and drain hatches also report how full they are; fluid and gas hatches count only their own kind of fluid, and they now read both the input and output tanks. Heat hatches report shell temperature. Redstone pauses reducers, boosters and relief valves as well as formed controllers. Feeding nitrogen, argon or inerts that the recipe does not need halves seal wear. Certificates only apply to machines that actually use them, including regulators, fluid loops, columns and charging pads: a certified column keeps its output and spends 25% less air. The electrolyzer must hold an electrode. Hazardous byproducts need a drain hatch. Dusty steam can scald but does not require a drain.
manual.workingmedium.page.17: This page covers the 0.2.4 changes. Sneak-use will not rotate a formed controller; break the shell if you really need to turn it, and a mid-batch break no longer wipes the recipe. Compressor and expander columns now drink lubricant and wear seals, and a certificate on them or on a charging station cuts air spent rather than slowing the machine. The electrolyzer can split water into hydrogen and oxygen. Dried kelp makes brine just like raw kelp. The crusher handles deepslate, cobbled deepslate, blackstone and netherrack. The probe reads pipe fittings and bound hatches. Keep hydrogen away from fire, and do not stand in dusty steam.
manual.workingmedium.page.2: The reducer drops one grade and turns the difference into heat. The booster spends four measures of low air for one measure of high air. The relief valve vents at the setpoint you sneak-use to choose. A redstone signal pauses a reducer, a booster or a relief valve so it stops transferring or venting. The gauge joins the network; sneak-use picks which grade it is judging.
manual.workingmedium.page.3: Controllers face away from you when placed. The structure grows in that direction. Towers stand on a 5x5 casing floor, then a 3x3 shaft of tray centers, a side hatch on every tray, and a head. A missing side draw floods the tower and stops it. Columns are vertical 3x3 jackets: stages stacked with intercoolers between them, capped at the top. Skip the intercooler and the next stage runs hot. Galleries are 3x3 tunnels of bays.
manual.workingmedium.page.4: The shell rating is the weakest casing. G5 casings hold the critical window; they are not a 120 bar line. Hatches replace casing. Item hatches, fluid hatches, a relief hatch and a drain are how a recipe moves. A recipe that produces acid, chlorine, caustic or flue gas will not start without a drain hatch. Item and fluid hatches also output a comparator signal for how full they are. A gas hatch reads the fuller of its input and output gases, and a fluid hatch does the same for liquids. A full output stops the machine. Nothing is voided for you.
manual.workingmedium.page.5: Impact crusher: 5x5x5 hollow shell, controller in the middle of the front face. It crushes cobblestone, stone, gravel, deepslate, cobbled deepslate, blackstone, netherrack, andesite, diorite, granite, tuff, basalt, calcite or end stone into stone dust; netherrack also drops a gold nugget. Silk-touched iron, copper and gold ore, including deepslate and nether gold, crush into two crushed ore. Silk-touched coal, redstone, lapis, diamond, emerald and nether quartz ore crush into a bonus of that drop, and glowstone, amethyst blocks and quartz blocks break back into four pieces. Four dust packs back into cobblestone, and the lube mixer can wet four dust with water to make clay. The cyclone is the same footprint but two blocks taller. Washer: a 5x5 base and at least six trays. Eight trays also drop a bonus nugget. The same washer can rinse gravel with water into flint and stone dust. Thermolysis wants a coil and makes two ingots from washed ore, plus slag and dusty steam. Ancient debris crushes the same way; the kettle then yields netherite scrap. From G1 on, put a seal in the seal slot or the machine starts to leak. The G0 crusher does not need a seal.
manual.workingmedium.page.6: Residue kiln turns crude oil into asphalt, heavy wax, metal ash and a little diesel. The same kiln also fires two sand or two red sand into three glass, two clay balls into three bricks, and two netherrack into three nether bricks. Lube mixer turns wax, plastic and water into PneumaticCraft lubricant. The same mixer also turns wax and water into plasticizer, stone dust and water into clay, and either kelp or dried kelp and water into brine. Four stone dust and one heavy wax also craft four asphalt on a bench, so you do not have to run the kiln just for a road. From G1 on, hot machines drink that lubricant. The flare burns hydrogen, flue gas, acid mist, chlorine and dusty steam, and puts that heat into its shell; it will not burn nitrogen, argon, oxygen or inerts. A nozzle in the special slot raises the burn rate.
manual.workingmedium.page.7: The fraction tower is the oil skyline. Eight trays split diesel, kerosene, gasoline and LPG. Taller trays add wax, acid feed and monomer. The cracker overheats into coke and stays coked until you sneak-use it, even if the temperature comes back or you briefly repair the shell. The polymerizer is exothermic: a large kettle without a relief hatch can throw a block. Put the catalyst in the catalyst slot; it stays there. Adding plasticizer raises the plastic yield from two to three. Leftover monomer or plasticizer can also be burned in the cycle island. Acid mist has to leave through a drain, or the machine will not start. The electrolyzer needs an electrode in the special slot.
manual.workingmedium.page.8: Leach turns washed ore and hydrochloric acid into metal solution, byproduct solution, acid mist and filter cake. Crystallizing the iron solution is the triple-yield step; washed copper and gold leach straight into three ingots. Ceramic alloy is steel, plastic and clay under oxygen in the alloy kettle. The quench well also grades alloys: LPG on compressed steel makes ceramic alloy, and liquid carbon dioxide on ceramic alloy makes cryo alloy. The same well can freeze a bucket of water with liquid carbon dioxide into packed ice, packed ice with more carbon dioxide into blue ice, and a bucket of lava with liquid carbon dioxide into two obsidian. The shell must survive 50 bar, so use G3 casings and industrial tube. The washer can also rinse crushed ancient debris into netherite scrap, with a gold nugget on an eight-tray tower, and can wash gravel into flint. The scrubber can also neutralize hydrochloric acid with caustic into brine.
manual.workingmedium.page.9: The compressor column is a vertical 3x3 stack. It pulls air from the block behind it and discharges higher pressure upward. At least four stages, with intercoolers between them. Each stage raises the pressure cap (10, 20, 50, 120 bar), limited by the weakest casing. A cylinder in the special slot multiplies how much air a compressor or expander moves. A certificate on a column cuts the air it spends by 25% while the output stays the same; a certified charging station likewise spends less air per charge, and does not charge more slowly. Columns are hot machines: they drink lubricant and wear a seal, and unused nitrogen in an input tank can purge them. The expander consumes high-pressure air and makes cold. Connect the cold end to the cryo tower with a heat gallery: the gallery carries heat between the block behind the controller and the block beyond the far cap, and a longer gallery transfers more slowly.
message.workingmedium.cannot_certify: This machine does not use a certificate.
message.workingmedium.certified: Certified %s. Air use and seal wear are reduced by 25%.
message.workingmedium.certify_unformed: The structure must be formed before it can be certified.
message.workingmedium.gate_closed: Expert catalog does not sell this
message.workingmedium.probe_duplicate: The bench already watches %s. Bind a different machine
message.workingmedium.probe_empty: The probe has no machine stored. Use it on a machine first
message.workingmedium.probe_missing: No machine at %s any more. Store it with the probe again
message.workingmedium.probe_unbound: This hatch is not bound to a formed machine.
message.workingmedium.rotate_formed: Sneak-use only rotates an unformed controller. Clear coke or freeze, or cycle a regulator, still works.
slot.workingmedium.special: Electrode, program, pump, slide, nozzle, cylinder, diaphragm or gripper
status.workingmedium.flood: A side draw is not connected
tooltip.workingmedium.asphalt: A paved road: walking on it is 35% faster.
tooltip.workingmedium.certificate: Use on a formed machine that spends air or moves a fluid or air stream to cut those costs by 25%. A certified column or charging station spends less air for the same work. Item galleries, heat galleries, flares and the calibration bench will not take it. The calibration bench can write more than one.
tooltip.workingmedium.cleaned: Cleaned. The critical kettle will accept this chip.
tooltip.workingmedium.curtain: Absorbs %s%% of damage while you wear a pneumatic chestplate
tooltip.workingmedium.cylinder: Place in a compressor or expander column to multiply air throughput by %s.
tooltip.workingmedium.diaphragm: Place in the regulator skid's special slot. %s%% of the inlet air reaches the outlet.
tooltip.workingmedium.dirty_chip: Dirty. Wash it in the clean room under pure nitrogen before the critical kettle will use it.
tooltip.workingmedium.electrode: Required in the electrolyzer special slot. Lasts %s batches.
tooltip.workingmedium.gripper: Place in a charging station or drone nest to multiply charge rate by %s.
tooltip.workingmedium.nozzle: Place in the flare's special slot to multiply burn rate by %s.
tooltip.workingmedium.probe: Use on a machine to store it for the calibration bench, on a bound hatch to store that controller, or on a reducer, booster, relief valve or gauge to read it.
tooltip.workingmedium.program_sheet: In the drone nest, also charges pneumatic items lying within four blocks.
tooltip.workingmedium.pump: In a fluid loop special slot, multiplies transfer rate by %s.
tooltip.workingmedium.slide: In an item gallery special slot, multiplies items moved by %s.
manual.workingmedium.page.18: This page covers the 0.2.5 changes. Gas hatches only drain gases and fluid hatches only drain liquids; if you were pulling the wrong kind through the wrong hatch, that line will stop. A charging station or drone nest now spends its per-tick budget on grade drills as well, so a drill in a slot charges at one point per tick unless a gripper speeds it up, and the pad shows not enough flow instead of sitting idle when it is short of air. The regulator skid gained 80 bar and 120 bar setpoints; older machines keep the setting they already had. Spilled hydrogen next to fire, lava or magma burns off. The crusher handles common stone types and silk-touched iron, copper and gold ore. The residue kiln fires sand into glass. The quench well freezes water into packed ice and packed ice into blue ice with liquid carbon dioxide. The cycle island can burn crude oil, with or without oxygen. Four stone dust and heavy wax craft asphalt. The scrubber neutralizes hydrochloric acid with caustic into brine.
manual.workingmedium.page.19: This page covers the 0.2.6 changes. A cracker that cokes, or a cryo tower that ices up, now stays down until you sneak-use it; coming back into the window or briefly repairing the shell no longer clears it by itself. Compressor and expander columns no longer drink lubricant or wear a seal on a tick that then fails for lack of air. Gas and fluid hatch comparators now read the fuller of the input and output tanks of that kind of fluid, so you can time extraction as well as filling. The G0 impact crusher no longer wears seals or leaks when the free seal life runs out. A charging pad will use the air it still has, even below 500, so long as one step can be paid. Spilled hydrogen also ignites next to a lit campfire, a soul campfire or a lava cauldron. The crusher handles silk-touched coal, redstone, lapis, diamond, emerald and nether quartz ore, and can break glowstone, amethyst blocks and quartz blocks back into four pieces. The residue kiln fires red sand into glass, clay into bricks and netherrack into nether bricks. The quench well turns lava and liquid carbon dioxide into obsidian. The washer rinses gravel into flint. Leftover monomer or plasticizer can be burned in the cycle island.
